scope: Measure retained structuredContent JSON values; do not infer negotiated protocol or output schema validity

sourceVerification.swift:
Apple Swift version 6.4 (swiftlang-6.4.0.34.1 clang-2100.3.34.1)
Target: arm64-apple-macosx27.0.0

nativeGUI.pidNote: No fresh original-App PID baseline was captured for this phase. An initial check incorrectly reused an older phase PID; no lifecycle stability claim is made.

checks: post-run checks exclude invalid/legacy pairs, retain all outcomes and reject incomplete v2 records
serialized media/truncation markers remain separate from native image blocks and text accounting in both encodings
local missing schema target diagnosed, valid/boolean/identified schemas not misreported; no tool call or reference leakage
root-declared cached Skill counted once with an informational layout hint and no mutation actions; extensionless references checked
latest cumulative counters, decreases and conflicts stay separate from requests and tools
separate Codex namespaces group with legacy MCP names; native images excluded and same-name outer tools stay distinct
structured JSON is measured separately from acknowledgment text; unavailable envelopes stay unknown and payloads are not exported
all JSON value shapes are measured, null differs from absence, array ranking recovers and returned-text accounting stays separate
CLI text and structured token order is declared in JSON, shared with human output, preserves metrics and keeps known zero before unknown

negativeDataRule: Non-JSON values remain unavailable; missing fields, null and unobservable results are distinct; old saved counters are not reconstructed without source logs
attemptNotes: Initial analyzer omitted --agent codex; preserved rejected-input outputs, corrected command and did not rerun SDK calls.
New non-JSON negative test exposed a Foundation Objective-C exception during fragment serialization. Fixed by validating the value inside an array before serialization; original failure log retained.
Existing diagnostic contract assumed every root-Skill issue had a local-reference target; updated exact expected issue codes to include the informational layout hint.

A lifecycle check incorrectly reused a prior phase original-App PID. No fresh PID baseline was captured, so no process-stability claim is made; selected configuration/App file hashes were verified instead.
limitations: SDK replies were re-encoded as owned Codex-format events, not actual native Codex session logs
365 targeted Debug tests, not full Release or x86_64 acceptance
JSON/reference counts do not establish prompt forwarding, model usage, billing, task success or tool quality
